parts.note: a steam train stops at every small station along the route, and a politician touring in the same way goes round giving short rousing speeches

explanation.surface: Someone stomping about venting their anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting off steam' suggests a temper, but it is a locomotive's steam, and 'going around' is a campaign trip with many brief stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign journey by train, with brief halts and speeches, is named after trains that halt only when signalled.

parts.note: a stop-order sounds like stock-market jargon, but these are wives or partners telling their husbands to stop

explanation.surface: Brokers placing stop-loss orders for friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop-orders' reads as finance; the mates are husbands being told to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Wives and girlfriends are the partners who tell their mates when to stop.

clue.text: Mood of Shakespeare bequeathing his second-best bed

definitions.text: Mood of Shakespeare bequeathing his second-best bed

parts.words: Mood of Shakespeare bequeathing his second-best bed
parts.note: Shakespeare's will left his wife only his second-best bed, so his testament seemed spiteful

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's feelings as he made his will.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's will famously left Anne Hathaway 'my second best bed'; the bard was Will, and so was the document.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or hostility is a mood, and the phrase also reads as an unkind testament.

clue.text: Work as journalist is up to that, but not a seaside water

definitions.text: that, but not a seaside water
definitions.note: the word in its old sense of time or season, as in eventide

indicators.note: is up in a down entry signals letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to edit is to work as a journalist on copy

explanation.surface: A journalist ready for the job but not for the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' reverses EDIT. The result is meant in its old sense of a time or season (Yuletide), not the sea's ebb and flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Old English used the word for a time or season, as in Whitsuntide, quite apart from the ocean's rise and fall.

clue.text: It may be by post — and fence

definitions.meaning: something sent inside a letter is an item enclosed in the post
a fence marks out a fenced-off area or paddock

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an item put in an envelope and a barrier or fenced area such as a racecourse paddock.

clue.text: Guarded the lodge, or the roof

definitions.meaning: a Freemasons' lodge is guarded by an officer called the tyler, so a guarded lodge is said to be tyled
a roof covered with slates or clay pieces

explanation.definitionFit: In Freemasonry a lodge is tyled when its door is guarded, and a roof is covered with clay or slate pieces.

parts.note: a desk's nest of small compartments is where letters are filed away to be dealt with later, and a bird's nesting hole is a nest

explanation.surface: A place where postponement lives.
explanation.walkthrough: A bird's nest and a desk compartment where unwanted papers are put off share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Desk compartments for papers, where business is shelved, are named after dovecote nesting holes.

definitions.note: noun standing for an adjective: relating to sight

indicators.note: made different, the letters of the clue word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A colliery looking unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges COALPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective concerns vision and the eye, so it means to do with sight.

clue.text: State how old you are for the press

definitions.note: what is written for newspapers: a noun

parts.note: to report is to state
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: A form asking a person's age for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is the verb, report.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalism, the reporting of news written for newspapers, is called this.

parts.note: air here is a tune, not the atmosphere, so the word wanted means relating to melody

explanation.surface: Something airborne or atmospheric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' reads as the sky; in music an air is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and the adjective describes what is tuneful or concerns melody.

clue.text: Call for strike after the loyal toast?

definitions.text: Call for strike after the loyal toast?

parts.words: Call for strike after the loyal toast
parts.note: at a formal British dinner nobody smokes until the toast to the monarch, after which the chair invites guests to strike matches and smoke

explanation.surface: A union leader calling a walkout at the end of a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks industrial; it is striking a match. The loyal toast is the toast to the King or Queen at a British formal dinner, after which smoking was allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an invitation to start smoking, the cigar-lighting signal after dinner.

parts.note: a spike driven into wood is struck on its head with a hammer, recalling the idiom about hitting it on the head

explanation.surface: A burglar knocked out by a householder.
explanation.walkthrough: The burglar picture is false: the thing that forces its way into timber is driven by a hammer blow to its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike forced into wood intrudes, and it is struck on the head to drive it.

definitions.note: the definition is what is said when one departs

parts.note: good is a mark of approval
byes are extras in cricket, runs scored without the ball touching the bat

explanation.surface: Bonuses signed off when an employee departs.
explanation.walkthrough: BYES are cricket extras: runs taken when the ball passes the batsman and the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewells are the words people say on departing.

indicators.note: backed tells us the word for a firm is written in reverse

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog with a business behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happen' is the definition; the firm is the usual crossword abbreviation, turned round by 'backed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come about or take place is a synonym of to happen.

parts.note: char is slang for tea, and the phrase for something that suits oneself is a personal cup of it

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady who pleases the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' suggests a charwoman (a British cleaner); it is slang for tea. Number One is oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something one likes very much means literally one's preferred brew.

clue.text: Will not yet come to flower on a note of opera

parts.note: Billy and Will are both short forms of William
a bud is a flower not yet open
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A man who has not yet blossomed, singing a note in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a verb; it is a name. Billy Budd is Britten's opera after Melville's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten's 1951 opera about a sailor is the stage work named here.

parts.note: rodeo horses buck, so their food would be something named for bucking; the plant is a marsh bogbean

explanation.surface: What rodeo horses eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant name is split as what bucking broncos would eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bogbean is a marsh plant, and its name splits into what bucking horses might eat.

clue.text: She found it stifling in Cyprus

definitions.text: She found it stifling in Cyprus

parts.words: She found it stifling in Cyprus
parts.note: in Othello the Moor smothers his wife in their bed in Cyprus

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker finding the island too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' looks like heat; in Shakespeare's Othello the heroine is smothered in Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife is smothered by him in the Cyprus scenes of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Aspiration to battle makes men jumpy aboard

definitions.note: a noun is wanted: the game in which pieces jump over each other on a board

parts.note: aspiration is the breathy h sound
the Alma was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War

explanation.surface: Breathless anticipation before a battle makes sailors on a ship nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' is read as 'a board': the men are pieces that jump on the board of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game where pieces leap over others, so its men are jumpy on a board.

clue.text: Army unit turns up fur coated

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: the creature wearing the fur

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company, an army unit

indicators.note: turns tells us the word up is written the other way round

explanation.surface: A regiment appears in fur coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fur coated' stands for an animal prized for its pelt; 'turns' acts on the little word 'up' beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American rodent, also called nutria, is farmed for its fur.

clue.text: "But the fool he called her his lady fair (Even as…)" (Kipling)

definitions.text: "But the fool he called her his lady fair (Even as…)" (Kipling)

parts.words: "But the fool he called her his lady fair (Even as…)" (Kipling)
parts.note: the missing words finish the refrain of Kipling's poem The Vampire, which compares the fool to the speaker and listener

explanation.surface: A line of Kipling's verse with its end blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in quotation: Kipling's poem The Vampire ends each verse with these three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's refrain says the fool was just like the speaker and the listener, the two of us.

clue.text: Wood work of curious style. Anne

indicators.note: curious, meaning odd, signals the letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Carpentry in an odd style by a woman called Anne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood work' looks like carpentry: it is a work by Mrs Henry Wood. 'curious' rearranges STYLE and ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen Wood, writing as Mrs Henry Wood, wrote the famous Victorian sensation novel of that title.

parts.note: Paradise Lost describes the lamps of Pandemonium as fed with this oil and asphaltus

explanation.surface: A line of Milton with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in quotation from Paradise Lost, Book I: the lamps were fed with the flammable oil and asphaltus.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton names this flammable oil as the fuel of Pandemonium's lamps.

definitions.meaning: Lewis Carroll wrote Sylvie and ..., whose boy hero bears the name
St ... founded the Carthusian order of monks

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the fairy boy in Lewis Carroll's Sylvie and Bruno and to the founder of the Carthusians.

definitions.meaning: sculptures of head and shoulders are statue-like pieces
a bender is a drinking spree, also called a bust

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sculpted heads and shoulders and drinking sprees.

clue.text: Mollusc offspring just over a foot

definitions.meaning: the young of oysters and other shellfish
a short gaiter covering the instep and ankle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the spawn of oysters and a short cloth gaiter worn over the shoe.

definitions.meaning: the sense whose organs are the buds on the tongue, or to touch them
discernment in matters of style and beauty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the sense perceived by the tongue's buds and refined judgment in aesthetics.

parts.note: succeeds means takes over, as to a title or estate, which needs no effort, merely birth

explanation.surface: A naturally gifted person who never makes an effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' reads as achieves; it means follows in a line of inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inherits takes over the title or estate by birth, without any effort.

clue.text: Indian currency setback caused by ecclesiastical dues

parts.note: the anna was a coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee
read as set back: the word set written backwards

explanation.surface: A drop in the rupee's value causes church taxes to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like a reverse; split it as 'set back', SET turned round to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Annates were the first year's income from a church living, paid to the Pope or Crown.

parts.note: a choice gives ELECT and an Academician RA, together naming Agamemnon's daughter Electra; the man wanted is her brother

explanation.surface: The sibling of a select member of the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: ELECT (choice) plus RA (Royal Academician) spells ELECTRA, and the answer is her brother in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Electra helped her brother avenge their father Agamemnon's murder.

parts.note: up and about suggests someone out of bed, but here it is a flight of steps that rises while winding round

explanation.surface: A patient recovered and back on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and about' means recovered, but the thing climbs upward while going round about a central post.
explanation.definitionFit: A helical flight of steps rises around a central column.
